explanation: XOR every index and every value, starting with n. Values present in both ranges cancel, leaving the missing member of 0 through n.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for n values. Each index and input value contributes one XOR in a single scan.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. Only the missing accumulator and loop index are retained.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: XOR is associative and each value XOR itself is zero. Every present member of 0..n appears once among the indices plus n and once among the array values, so it cancels. Only the missing member occurs once and remains.
walkthrough: For [4,0,1,3], n=4. XOR the full range {0,1,2,3,4} with the input values {4,0,1,3}. All shared values cancel, leaving 2.
edgeCases: The missing value may be zero or n.
Values are distinct and lie in 0..n.
